artifacts.summary: Five-phase plan ruling option (2) and fixing the --cached untracking shape end-to-end in git-commit-scoped.sh, with regression tests, documentation, and a full-gate redeploy.

memory_candidates.content: git commit -- <pathspec> has --only semantics and re-reads the working tree for each named path at commit time. A consequence verified empirically across four variants: a 'git rm --cached <dir>' untracking whose content REMAINS on disk cannot be committed by ANY pathspec-scoped form -- a directory pathspec, an explicit HEAD-tracked file list, and 'git commit --only -- <files>' all exit 1 ('nothing to commit') with HEAD unmoved. Only a bare 'git commit' (whole index) lands the deletion. Pathspec granularity is irrelevant; the constraint is in --only semantics. Any scoped-commit wrapper that must support untracking therefore needs a guarded bare-commit path proven index-equivalent to the declared pathspec set (compare 'git diff --cached --name-only HEAD' against the same restricted to the declared pathspecs, using git's own resolver so :(exclude) entries are honored), not a widened pathspec predicate.
